The composed devices — greyscale

Every house, realm and place the archive routes a device for — and every one it does not.

Drawn under ruling C92, and this sheet was rebuilt to it. An earlier sheet drew every generated device in open line inside a broken frame, under C64. C92 withdrew that frame: a forged device is drawn properly, in the hall's full visual language, and the glyph carries the distinction — the frame would have been a sixth signal for something ◆ already says. 33 of the 62 drawings on the old sheet carried a dashed rim and neither it nor its dataset contained the word basis or the mark ◆ anywhere. This one carries both, and no drawing on it is dashed.

The half of C64 that survives is the declared blank. Where the lore will not support a device the corner stays bare and says why — the hall's ○ class, “the field is left bare rather than filled in”. All 10 of them are below, each with the measured reason, and not one has been filled in to make the sheet look finished.

A device Tolkien designed is shown as the hall's own file and is never redrawn. Every ✔ corner below is the same image the Hall of Heraldry serves — 17 of the 152 distinct devices resolve to a recreation held under site/heraldry/, and an approximation is never put in a recreation's place. Every one of them resolved; none was silently forged.

The remaining 135 are drawn by the Hall of Heraldry's own forge, ardaForgeDevice in site/heraldry.js, from the same spec the hall renders — not by a second drawing tool. Its constants are measured off Tolkien's own plates rather than assumed. No artwork of Tolkien's or Christopher Tolkien's is reproduced and no lettering of his is drawn at any size; what the archive takes from a plate is measurement and not image.

Two axes are recorded and they are not one axis. The glyph is basis and answers how the archive came to have the picture. The bracketed mark is confidence and answers how strong the evidence is that this subject bears it: [C] the corpus names the charge as a device of this subject · [I-H] it attests the image but not as heraldry, or attests it for the parent of a branch · [I-M] a longer chain. A device Tolkien drew himself can be attached to a subject at [I-H], and a subject the corpus names outright can bear a picture the archive had to interpret. Neither is derived from the other.

Counted: 218 subjects · 208 carry a device, sharing 152 distinct drawings · 10 carry none.
✔ a device Tolkien designed — shown as the recreation the Hall of Heraldry holds, the file itself, never redrawn here✦ a device Tolkien drew, which cannot be reproduced here — forged from his recorded description and from arrangements and inks measured off the plates✧ blazoned in the texts and never drawn by anyone◆ the archive's own interpretation, where Tolkien left no device○ no device is recorded anywhere — the field is left bare rather than filled in

Silvan (companion of Nimrodel)
No attested device, no attested image, and no declared link to either. The archive's own tier-1 ceiling says why this is the commonest answer: `except for the descriptions in The Fall of Gondolin, and that of the badge of Finarphin in The Lay of Leithian and elsewhere, references to Elvish heraldic devices are rare and brief in Tolkien's works`. The evidence sweep found CO-OCCURRENCE ONLY: a blazon word standing near the name with nothing binding the two. On its own that supports a declared blank as readily as it supports a device.
